Leo Lemuel.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Imperial Guard Sergeant|Sergeant]] of the [[Imperial Guard]] closely tied to [[Lord Solar]] [[Macharius]] during the [[Macharian Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
Hailing from the [[Hive World]] of [[Belial (Hive World)|Belial]], Leo and his comrades [[Ivan]] and [[Antoniev]] joined the Imperial Guard in order to escape the constant gang warfare of their world. He soon became a tank driver on the [[Baneblade]] ''Indomitable'' in the [[7th Belial]] [[Regiment]].{{Fn|1a}}

Leo and the ''Indomitable'' were deployed to [[Karsk IV]] in the early days of the [[Macharian Crusade]], and during the fighting their tank commander [[Lieutenant]] [[Doblinsky]] was killed. Leo, Ivan, and Anton along with two new recruits were the sole survivors of their tank crew.{{Fn|1b}} They next were assigned to take part in the securing of the city of Irongrad and battled the [[Cult of the Angel of Fire]], during which he enters a relationship with an [[Imperial Assassin]] dubbed [[Anna]] who in truth working for [[Inquisitor]] [[Hyronimus Drake]] and was disguised as a nurse.{{Fn|1c}} Through Anna, the group are assigned to guard the wounded [[Lord Commander]] [[Macharius]] at a hospital.{{Fn|1d}} During an attack on the city by [[Cultist]]s, Leo and his squad protected the wounded Macharius{{Fn|1e}} and helped Macharius in defeating the [[Lord of Change]] at the heart of the Cult. For their heroism, Macharius appointed Leo and his squad to his bodyguard unit.{{Fn|1f}}

Serving for the next ten years in Macharius' personal guard, Lemuel became embroiled in the battle against the [[Dark Eldar]] for control of the [[Fist of Russ|Fist of Demetrius]] after their ship ''[[Lux Imperatoris]]'' was lost in a [[Warp Storm]] and raided by the [[Xenos]].{{Fn|2a}} Fighting alongside Macharius, Drake, and [[Space Wolves]] under [[Ulrik Grimfang]] and [[Logan Grimnar]] they managed to drive the Xenos back from the ''Lux Imperatoris'', though they escaped with the Fist.{{Fn|2b}} Leo accompanied Macharius to [[Procrastes]] and then into the [[Webway]] in pursuit of the Dark Eldar Lord [[Ashterioth]], who sought to use the Fist to reach the [[Reality Engine]].{{Fn|2c}} During the final battle, Leo threw a [[grenade]] at Ashterioth which destabilized his connection to the engine, and before the Xenos could kill him he was saved by the intervention of [[Macharius]] and [[Logan Grimnar]].{{Fn|2d}}

Lemuel's service with Macharius went all the way to the last days of the Crusade on [[Loki (Macharian Crusade)|Loki]], where he and Ivan were becoming demoralized by the bitter plague-ridden conflict.{{Fn|3a}} During the conflict, he contracted a mysterious illness which gave him horrifying hallucinations.{{Fn|3b}} He is taken to a [[Sisters Hospitaller]] hospital on Loki to recover, where he seemingly reunites with Anna, who he begins to suspect may be something else entirely.{{Fn|3c}} After returning to Macharius' side, he witnessed the political turmoil of the final days of the Crusade, where the sickly Macharius was now the victim of constant plots by his own Generals and advisors.{{Fn|3d}}

During the final battle on Loki, Lemuel accompanies Macharius for the final attack on the Traitor General [[Richter (Macharian Crusade)|Richter]]'s stronghold. Leo is again given control of a [[Baneblade]].{{Fn|3e}} Battling through [[Daemon]]s and other horrors, Lemuel survives the final battle as Richter is defeated, but learns afterwards that Anna was a [[Callidus Assassin]] now impersonating a [[Inquisitorial Stormtrooper]] and had killed both Macharius and Drake. The assassin claimed that Macharius was already close to death, and the assassination on the behalf of unknown parties was an act of mercy to preserve his legacy and heroism. The assassin let Leo live to let him tell the "official" version of Macharius death.{{Fn|3f}}

Leofric.wikitext:
{{GreyKnightsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Grey Knights]] [[Justicar]] who led his squad to the [[Calaphrax Cluster]], after the [[Chapter]]'s [[Prognosticator (librarian)|Prognosticator]]s warned that [[Daemonic]] activity was going to occur somewhere within the Cluster.

==Biography==
[[Image:Leofric.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Justicar {{PAGENAME}}]]
'''Leofric''' and his squad of [[Grey Knights Terminators]] were sent to the [[Calaphrax Cluster]] with a [[Grey Knights Strike Cruiser|Strike Cruiser]] when the [[Prognosticator (librarian)|Prognosticator]]s foretold of [[Daemon]]ic activity after the [[warp storm]]s that had shrouded the region for ten thousand years abated. As the Prognosticators were unable to fully perceive the region due to after-effects of the warp storm, Leofric decided to meet with [[Inquisitor]] [[Sabbathiel]], who was already in the Cluster and had requested an audience with the Grey Knights. The Inquisitor had claimed that the [[Dark Angels]] [[Chapter]] were [[heretic]]s and after Leofric demanded proof, Sabbathiel listed her evidence against them - much of it from her encounters with the Dark Angels within the Calaphrax Cluster itself. Once Sabbathiel was finished, Leofric conversed with his squadron and was convinced that the Inquisitor's accusation had merit and agreed to confront the forces of [[Space Marine Captain|Master]] [[Seraphus]] in the Cluster. The Justicar and Inquisitor's ships then located Master Seraphus' warship and Leofric demanded that he allow them to board, so they could carry out their investigation to determine if the Dark Angels were heretics.{{fn|1}}

Leonas.wikitext:
{{DeathwatchPortal}}
''''Last' Leonas''' is a [[Deathwatch]] member of [[Watch Station]] [[Picket's Watch]] and believes himself to be the soul survivor of the [[Black Consuls]] [[Chapter]]. 

==History==
This occurred after the [[Siege of Goddeth Hive]], which annihilated the Black Consuls - save for Leonas and six others, who were elsewhere when the battle took place. The seven believed themselves to be the only surviving Black Consuls left and, though, they briefly discussed rebuilding their Chapter, they ultimately decided against doing so. Instead all seven vowed to permanently join the Deathwatch and Leonas served aboard Picket's Watch. As the centuries passed, however, his surviving battle brothers fell in combat, until in 999.M41 only Leonas remained. It was at that time he began to refer to himself as the ''''Last'''' and swore an oath to survive no matter the odds that were against him in battle - as with his death, the Black Consuls would die as well. He would frequently inform his fellow Death Watch [[Battle Brothers]] of this as well, and they too began to refer to Leonas as the Last{{Fn|1a}}. However, he would come close to breaking his oath, when Leonas and his [[Kill-Team]] '''Orion''' were charged with raiding one of the [[Tau Empire]]'s traveling emissary crafts in space{{Fn|1b}}. In doing so, Picket's Watch hoped some of the craft's technology would hold information, on where the newly created [[Stormsurge]] [[Battlesuit]]s, being used in the [[Third Sphere of Expansion|Agrellan Campaign]], were coming from{{Fn|1a}}. Using the [[Strike Cruiser]] [[Robidoux]]{{Fn|1b}}, they boarded the Tau craft with a [[Thunderhawk]], and expected an easy mission, but they were unaware that an [[Ethereal]] was aboard the craft. This caused the Ethereal [[Fire Warrior]] bodyguards to fight fiercely to protect the Tau leader and though the Kill-Team was successful in their mission, the Xenos shot down their Thunderhawk before they could escape. With no chance now of returning to their Strike Cruiser, the Kill-Team vowed to take down as many of the Tau as they could before dying. They would go on to take a heavy toll on the Fire Warriors, but the Kill-Team was killed one by one, until only Leonas remained. He would fight on, but was soon hit by a massive explosion and was embraced by darkness...{{Fn|1c}} 

Leonas had thought he had died, but instead he was surprised to wake up imprisoned by the Tau, though he was left heavily wounded by the battle. The Tau then had [[Human]] [[Gue'vesa]] members of their forces talk to Leonas and try to convince him to embrace the [[Greater Good]] and join the [[Tau Empire]]. He would refuse, however, and a series of Gue'vesa would then try to mentally break him down, with psychological verbal attacks and threats of physical violence. Leonas would whether it all, though, until the Tau sent in one final Gue'vesa, named [[Guilliman|Roboute]], who told the Black Consul, that this was his last chance and he would be jettisoned out of an air-lock into space, if he did not join the Tau Empire. Leonas did not hesitate to refuse once again, but before the Tau could carry out their threat, the emissary craft was attacked{{Fn|1c}} by the Deathwatch. Luckily for Leonas, the Strike Cruiser Robidoux had been able to send a message, that his Kill-Team had been stranded aboard the Tau craft, to the Watch Station Picket's Watch, before contact was lost with the ship. Picket's Watch would receive the message and this allowed [[Watch Captain]] [[Nergui]]{{Fn|1b}} to track the Tau craft down and attack it with his Strike Cruiser [[Nemesis (Strike Cruiser)|Nemesis]]. As Nergui's Kill-Team then boarded the Tau craft{{Fn|1d}}, Leonas freed himself during the attack and killed Roboute{{Fn|1c}}, before then joining up with Nergui's forces. After informing them that the rest of his Kill-Team was dead{{Fn|1d}}, Leonas and the Deathwatch marines made their escape back to the Nemesis with some of the Tau's technology they had captured{{Fn|1a}}. The information they gathered from the Tau's tech, informed them that the Stormsurges were coming from the abandoned [[Imperial]] world [[Proth]] and the Death Watch began planning to attack it{{Fn|1e}}. Leonas would be among the Death Watch's forces, that later successfully destroyed the Tau Empire's M'Yan'Ral Stormsurge facility, on Proth.{{Fn|1f}}

Leonatos.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[Chapter]], sent on a Bloodquest to atone for a failure.{{fn|1b}}

==History==
{{Spoiler|source=Bloodquest (Graphic Novel Series)}}
====Origins====
A native of Baal, Leonatos went against other would-be aspirants in the '''Ritual of Challenge''' and earned a place among the "Sky Warriors". In less than half a century, he was chosen to command a [[Space Marine Company|Company]] of Astartes.{{fn|1a}}
====The Blade Encarmine====
Over a century after his induction, Leonatos was sent by [[Chapter Master|Commander]] [[Dante]] to defend a warp-station of the [[Adeptus Astronomica]] from an [[Ork]] assault.{{fn|1a}} To aid him in this task, the Captain was entrusted with the [[Blade Encarmine]], a [[Power sword]] gifted by [[Primarch]] [[Sanguinius]] to [[Belarius]] ten millennia earlier. After five days and nights of fierce fighting, with hardly 30 Astartes still alive out of the 100 who made planetfall, Leonatos challenged the [[Warboss]], killing him but losing the sword to the raiders in the process.{{fn|1b}}
====The Destroyer====
In the ensuing trial, Leonatos was condemned to exile until he came back with the sword. Accompanied by several battle-brothers and their company's [[Chapter Serf|blood thralls]] aboard the ship ''Exile''. The Blood Angels followed the trail of the Ork warband{{fn|1c}}, facing [[Daemon]]s{{fn|1d}}, [[Chaos Space Marine|traitor Astartes]] pirates{{fn|1e}}, and mutants{{fn|1f}} on the way. Their quest led them to the world of [[Leptis]], under attack by [[Waaagh!]] [[Gharshûl]], whose leader was said to be in possession of the Blade Encarmine. The Exiles boarded the warlord's flagship, hoping to behead the Ork force and recover their prize. However, they found out that Garshûl was actually possessed by a daemon intent on finding a new vessel in Leonatos. The Blood Angels vanquished the [[Daemonhost]], which revealed the sword was in its master's possession in the [[Eye of Terror]].{{fn|1g}}
====Eidolon====
As the ''Exile'' was wrecked by the [[Warp]], the Astartes find themselves on the [[Daemon World]] of [[Eidolon (Daemon World)|Eidolon]].{{fn|2a}}{{fn|2b}} After being guided by one of [[The Fallen]] named [[Haeroth|Haeroth the Damned]], they set out to overcome the servants of [[Chaos]] that stood in the way of their quest.{{fn|2c}} Across the realms of Eidolon, their numbers grew fewer as brother after brother was lost to the powers of [[Khorne]]{{fn|2d}}{{fn|2e}}, [[Nurgle]]{{fn|2f}}{{fn|2g}}, and [[Slaanesh]]{{fn|2h}}{{fn|2i}}. In the Labyrinth of [[Tzeentch]], Leonatos and his two remaining compatriots faced Haeroth and his master, which had promised its servant freedom if he brought the Blood Angels captain to serve as a daemonhost.{{fn|2j}}{{fn|2k}} They overcame the Fallen and gained possession of the Blade, but the former master unleashed legions of daemons and Leonatos hurled the sword to his comrades before being swarmed by the warp creatures.{{fn|2l}}
====Lost====
After bringing the Blade back to Baal, the two surviving Exiles endeavored the look for their captain.{{fn|3a}}{{fn|3b}} Journeying across the galaxy and pretending to join a band of traitor Astartes{{fn|3c}}{{fn|3d}}, they discovered that Leonatos had become a daemonhost at the head of a new [[Black Crusade]]{{fn|3e}}. Using the captain's martial acumen, the daemon planned to lay waste to undefended worlds of the Imperium.{{fn|3f}} Leonatos then watched with cruel delight as he forced the captured Exiles to duel each other to death, promising an agonizing corruption by Chaos to the survivor.{{fn|3g}} Relying on his erstwhile comrades' abilities{{fn|3h}}, Leonatos managed to briefly regain control of his body and direct the Chaos fleet towards an Imperial ambush before the daemon took over again.{{fn|3i}} Anticipating the Exiles' moves, the daemonhost faced one of them as he attempted to sabotage the flagship's war field generators.{{fn|3j}} When the Exile gained the upper hand, Leonatos managed to regain control one last time to explain the trick he played on his tormentor. Declaring himself to be free, he let his subordinate go as he was destroyed along with the Chaos fleet.{{fn|3k}}

Leonid Osma.wikitext:
{{InquisitionPortal}}
'''Leonid Osma''' was an [[Inquisitor]] of the [[Ordo Malleus]] and a member of the [[Ordos Helican]], which policed the entire [[Helican Subsector]]. He was believed to be a shoe-in for becoming [[Inquisitor#Ranks|Grandmaster]] of the Ordos Helican, a role which he had spent his whole life chasing, and which he finally attained when Grandmaster [[Orsini]] died. He is perhaps best known for his part in the [[Eisenhorn]] Conspiracy, a role which eventually led to his death.

Osma was a well-built broad-shouldered man, with a blunt and pugnacious face. He lost his lower jaws during a fight with a [[Khorne Berzerker]] and had since replaced it with bionics. His weapon is a [[power weapon|power hammer]], the symbol of his Ordo.

==History==
===The Eisenhorn Conspiracy===
[[File:Osma.jpeg|thumb|Osma and his retinue arrive on [[Cadia]]{{fn|1a}}]]
In 339.M41, Osma arrested Inquisitor Gregor Eisenhorn of the [[Ordo Xenos]] on [[Cadia]] on charges of a carta extremis while the latter was on the trail of the Heretic [[Inquisitor]] [[Quixos]]. Osma declared him [[Extremis Diabolus]] and had him imprisoned within the Carnificina. Among the charges against him were daemonancy and committing the [[Thracian Primaris]] atrocity. After three months of Eisenhorn being interrogated by Osma's staff, words arrived at the Carnificina that [[Lord Inquisitor]] [[Rorken]] had persuaded Grandmaster [[Orsini]] to have him extradited to [[Thracian Primaris]], where he would stand trial before a [[Magistery Tribunal]] of the [[Ordo Malleus]] and the [[Officio of Internal Prosecution]]. On the night before the Black Ships arrived to take Eisenhorn to Thracian, Eisenhorn's retinue broke him out of the Carnificina, and they fled aboard the [[Rogue Trader]] [[Maxilla]]'s ship, the Essene, whose service Eisenhorn had previously hired. Eisenhorn later cleared his name by tracking down and killing Quixos with the help of five other Inquisitors.

When Osma next met Eisenhorn, he had risen to the rank of Grandmaster. This time, Godwyn Fischig, fearing that Eisenhorn had fallen to damnation, had sold him out to Osma in an attempt to redeem his friend. With Fischig's assistance, Osma and fellow Inquisitor [[Heldane]], accompanied by [[Stormtrooper]]s, boarded the Essene and apprehended Eisenhorn. Osma demanded that Eisenhorn hand over the [[daemonhost]] [[Cherubael]] and the forbidden text [[Malus Codicium]], but was interrupted by the arrival of [[Cherubael]], who had been summoned by Eisenhorn's savant [[Aemos]] into the body of one of [[Maxilla]]'s [[astropath]]s. Cherubael easily dispatched the stormtroopers, and nearly killed Heldane. The enraged Osma attacked Eisenhorn with his power hammer, thinking that he had summoned the daemon. Before Osma could deliver the killing blow, Maxilla shot him in the back of the head with his digital ring weapon and killed him.

Osma's death was never confirmed by Eisenhorn, and the Inquisition declared him KIA some time later. Why Heldane, who survived, never revealed the nature of his master's death to his superiors is unknown. Lord Rorken succeeded Osma as Grandmaster of the Ordos Helican after his disappearance.

Leopold Cronus.wikitext:
{{ImperialKnightsPortal}}
'''Leopold Cronus'''{{Fn|1a}} was a studious [[House Taranis]] [[Imperial Knight|Knight]], who commanded the Knight suit ''[[Pax Mortis]]'' and he took part in the [[Great Crusade]]{{Fn|1b}} and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1b}} 

==Biography==
He was close comrades with his fellow [[House Taranis]] [[Imperial Knight|Knight]] [[Raf Maven]] and the two earned great glory for themselves on the [[Great Crusade]]'s battlefields{{Fn|1b}}. Both were later present on [[Mars]], when the [[Horus Heresy]] began and the [[Dark Mechanicum]] caused a [[Schism of Mars|civil war]] to erupt on their Homeworld. House Taranis would remain [[Loyalist|loyal]] to the [[Imperium]]{{Fn|1c}} and the two younger Knights, would serve under the more experienced Knight [[Stator]]'s command{{Fn|1b}}, as they fought against the [[Traitor]]s. This changed, however, when House Taranis decided to defend [[Adept]] [[Koriel Zeth]]'s [[Forge Temple|forge]], [[Magma City]], from the Dark Mechanicum's forces. With several of their Knights left inoperable at that time, the House's Knights had to deploy in teams of two. This led Stator to depart from Maven and Cronus and he instead partnered with the less experienced [[Gentran]], who had only recently been elevated to Knighthood{{Fn|1c}}. 

While the two patrolled Magma City, though, [[Raf Maven|Maven]]'s [[Auspex]] sensed the [[Dark Mechanicum]] [[Kaban Machine|war machine]] that had attacked them earlier in the conflict and nearly killed him. An enraged Maven vowed to destroy it and while Cronus was doubtful that the war machine had survived its battle with Maven, he agreed to join the hunt for it and the two departed without notifying their Household{{Fn|1d}}. They began tracking down signs of the machine and it was after they discovered a destroyed mag-line train, that Cronus realized Maven had been right and vowed to help him destroy the war machine. It was at that time that both Knights discovered that the [[Schism of Mars]] had begun in earnest, and open warfare between the supporters of [[Horus]] and the [[Emperor]] had fully spread across their Homeworld. Despite this, the two continued their hunt{{Fn|1e}} and later discovered the war machine deep within the region of [[Mars]], known as the [[Noctis Labyrinthus]], where the war machine was about to fire upon a group of terrified [[Mechanicum]] servants. Acting quickly, Maven and Cronus worked together to bury the war machine in rubble and Maven personally destroyed the machine by plunging his Knight's sword deep within it. The two Knights were then approached by the Transcriber [[Dalia Cythera]], who had been among the Mechanicum group the Knights had just saved. Using a [[Cult of the Dragon|mysterious power]] she possessed, Cythera healed{{Fn|1f}} the two damaged Knights and told them of a remote hidden automated research facility, owned by [[Tech Adept|Adept]] [[Koriel Zeth]]. She told them to go there and wait for Mar's civil war to end and under the sway of Cythera's power, the two Knights did as she commanded.{{Fn|1h}}

Leops Franck.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Master of the Astronomican]] and a [[High Lord of Terra]], during the fifth year of the [[13th Black Crusade]].  Franck was one of the High Lords which opposed [[Chancellor of the Imperial Council]] [[Lev Tieron|Lev Tieron's]] attempt to push through a Dissolution act that would free the [[Adeptus Custodes]] from their vows on [[Terra]].{{Fn|1}}

Leops Franck was one of the key architects of a plan to use the [[Dark Eldar]] to repair the failing [[Golden Throne]].{{Fn|3}} Along with [[Lord Inquisitor]] [[Adamara Rassilo]], [[Speaker for the Chartist Captains]] [[Kania Dhanda]], and [[Fabricator-General]] [[Oud Oudia Raskian]] a scheme was conducted to smuggle a Dark Eldar [[Haemonculus]] onto Terra to repair the Throne, but it escaped and began to instead run amok where it was eventually killed by Inquisitor [[Erasmus Crowl]] and [[Custodes]] under [[Navradaran]].{{Fn|2}} Despite this setback, Franck was able to organize a delegation to travel to an unspecified location (likely [[Commorragh]]) and finish the final phase of the negotiations with the Dark Eldar. He was eventually confronted in the [[Hollow Mountain]] by Erasmus Crowl, and in the ensuing battle Franck used his formidable psychic abilities to nearly kill the Inquisitor. However the [[Astronomican]] malfunctioned during the battle as the [[Noctis Aeterna]] approached, creating a blast that sent Franck over a cliff.{{Fn|3}} Franck was killed, with the High Lords apaprently thinking he was slain in a calamity that befall the Astronomican. He was replaced by [[Lucius Throde]].{{Fn|4}}

Lerod.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Lerod''' was a [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]], commanding one of the [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment's]] [[platoon]]s.{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
Prior to enlisting with the [[Astra Militarum]], Lerod was the commander of the [[Tanith Ultima]] [[PDF|Militia]]. As a result of being brought up in Tanith's shrine city, he and the [[Trooper]]s under his command were some of the most devout and pious in the entire regiment.{{Fn|1a}} The regiment's commander, [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]], considered Lerod a gifted and loyal officer.{{Fn|1b}}

By the time of the regiment's action on [[Monthax]], Lerod had been assigned command of Seven Platoon{{Fn|2}} (the original incarnation of Seven Platoon having been wiped out on [[Menazoid Epsilon]] by the treacherous [[Jantine First|Jantine Patricians]]).{{Fn|1c}} While fighting on Monthax, Lerod suffered a psychological break from reality, believing himself to be untouchable after surviving a number of assaults by [[Chaos Cultists]] completely unscathed. Ironically, Lerod was the only Guardsman killed in the Tanith's last phase of the campaign, taking a lucky shot while fighting on the roof an ancient [[Aeldari]] temple.{{Fn|2}}

Lexell Kotov.wikitext:
{{AdeptusMechanicusPortal}}
[[Image:LexellKotov.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Archmagos Lexell Kotov{{Fn|4}}]]
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an [[Archmagos]] [[Explorator]] of the [[Adeptus Mechanicus]].{{Fn|1}}

Kotov was originally the [[Fabricator-General]] of a series of [[Forge World]]s. However by late [[M41]] Kotov had been beset by a series of misfortunes. His Forge World of [[Arcetri]] was consumed by [[Tyranids]] while another, [[Uraniborg 1572]], was lost to the [[Dark Mechanicus]] under the [[Heretek]] [[Votheer Tark]]. To compound this, Kotov next lost his Forge World of [[Palomar]] when he attempted to resurrect the buried [[Ark Mechanicus]] ''[[Speranza]]'', which caused a violent chain reaction across the planet. While he had lost his last Forge World, he had nonetheless aquired the ''Speranza''. This vessel was his last hope, and Kotov sought to reverse his fortunes by discovering the lost expedition of [[Vettius Telok]] and the fabled [[Breath of the Gods]].{{Fn|1}}

Kotov was able to muster his remaining forces to form the modestly sized [[Kotov Crusade]] in search of Telok's expedition on the other side of the [[Halo Stars|Halo Scar]].{{Fn|1a}} After a long and difficult journey in search of Telok, the remaining elements of the Crusade managed to reach the world of [[Exnihilo]] and Kotov came face to face with Telok.{{Fn|2}} However it soon became apparent that Telok had become mad and intended to use the Breath of the Gods to destroy [[Terra]] and [[Mars]] in order to rule as the new [[Emperor]].{{Fn|3}} Accepting help from the [[Eldar]] of [[Biel-Tan]] under [[Farseer]] [[Bielanna Faerelle]], Kotov and Telok's forces engaged in a vicious battle over Exnihilo.{{Fn|3a}} The final battle took place aboard the ''Speranza'' itself as Telok attempted to gain control of the semi-sentient vessel in order to use it to reach the [[Sol System]] with the Breath of the Gods. Kotov and Telok engaged in a digital battle of the minds aboard the ''Speranza's'' system. Thanks to Kotovs allies and the ''Speranza'' itself siding with him, Kotov was able to purge Telok's mind and prevail.{{Fn|3b}}

In the aftermath of the battle nearly all of the Humans and Eldar of the Kotov Crusade were now dead, but Kotov and the survivors were able to limp back to [[Imperial]] space with the ''Speranza''. He returned to Imperial in search of new beginnings.{{Fn|3c}}

Leyr.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Leyr''' was a [[Imperial Guard Scout|Scout]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]].{{Fn|2a}}


==Biography==
One of the original [[Tanith]] members of the regiment, prior to enlisting with the [[Astra Militarum]] Leyr was a member of the [[Tanith Magna]] [[PDF|militia]]. He initially held the rank of [[Trooper]].{{Fn|1a}}

When the Tanith First were deployed on [[Hagia]], Leyr took part in the fighting to retake the [[Holy Doctrinopolis]]. At one point, Leyr, [[Yael (Tanith)|Yael]] and [[Gol Kolea|Kolea]] accompanied [[Colonel]] [[Colm Corbec|Corbec]] in a flanking manoeuvre on a guild hall that had been fortified as a holdout for some [[Infardi]] [[Chaos Cultists|cultists]]. However, although the Tanith were able to infiltrate the hall through a disused basement, there were more cultists than they expected. Corbec and Yael were captured and Leyr was shot in the thigh, but Kolea managed to save his life and get him to [[Medic]] [[Tolin Dorden|Dorden]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}

Later, by the time of the regiment's deployment on [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]] in '''771.[[M41]]''', Leyr had been elevated to the ranks of the Tanith First's elite [[Imperial Guard Scout|scout]] corps.{{Fn|2a}} He was now attached to the [[Imperial Guard Platoon|third platoon]] under [[Major]] [[Elim Rawne|Rawne]].{{Fn|2b}}

Lhora Craft.wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
[[Image:Lhora_Craft_Model.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lhora Craft{{Fn|1d}}]]
A renowned "Archeotechnologist" in [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]'s [[underhive]], '''Lhora Craft''' is known among traders as first rate finder of lost [[archeotech]] in the underhive.{{Fn|1}}

==History==
Born to a [[House Craft|wealthy noble family]] as the daughter of [[Augustus Craft|Count Augustus Craft]], Lhora displayed a rebellious streak in her youth against her harsh father. She spent much of her younger years confining herself to her chambers, studying and developing a fascination of the mysteries of technology and the [[Cult Mechanicus|spiritual religion]] surrounding it. Lhora grew tired of the lavish decadence of noble life and once she came of age she quietly escaped her noble house. She now lives in the underhive, keeping her noble identity a secret, making her living off selling rediscovered archeotech {{Fn|1a}}. Occasionally, she finds employment as a [[Hired Gun|hired gun]] for various [[Gang|underhive gangs]] on Necromunda on missions where there is the prospect of loot and technology to acquire, though she refuses to work with [[Spyrer|Spryer Hunters]], [[Scavvies]], [[Redemption Cult|Redemptionists]], and [[House Cawdor|Cawdor gangs]] {{Fn|1b}}

==Appearance and Abilities==
Despite its outwardly thin appearance, Lhora's outfit contain many hidden pockets which allow her to deftly switch through various weapons in combat. She is proficient in any weapon that can be found in the underhives of Necromunda, and is known to carry a [[Necron]] pistol weapon as well as a variety of [[Master-crafted weapon|Master-crafted weapons]]. She is a deftly agile person and able to make significant leaps for a baseline human.{{Fn|1c}}

*[[Wikipedia:Ian Livingstone|Sir Ian Livingstone]], one of the co-founders of [[Games Workshop]], would also later become the president of [[Wikipedia:Eidos Interactive|Eidos Interactive]], the company which created the ''Tomb Raider'' video game and franchise.

'''Lhorke''', known as '''The First''' was a [[Dreadnought]] of the [[World Eaters]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
The former Legion Master before the discovery of [[Angron]] when they were still known as the War Hounds, Lhorke was gravely injured on the world of [[Jeracau]] but interred within a Dreadnought suit. He was perhaps the first Dreadnought of the World Eaters legion, and led a unit of other early prototype Dreadnoughts. During the [[Ghenna Massacre]] Lhorke was reawoken by [[Mago]] who feared that Angron would soon install the [[Butcher's Nails]] throughout the Legion. Lhorke took part in Mago's failed rebellion, but upon the [[Centurion (Rank)|Centurion]]'s death by [[Kharn]] bent the knee to Angron.{{Fn|2}} Spared the Butcher's Nails implants due to his Dreadnought status, Lhorke watched as his War Hounds descended into a force of brutal murderers and madmen. However what horrified Lhorke most of all was the slaughter of his fellow World Eaters during the [[Battle of Isstvan III]]. Nonetheless he remained loyal to his Legion and his [[Primarch]].{{Fn|1b}}

Later during the [[Shadow Crusade]], Lhorke battled alongside [[Librarian]] [[Vorias]]. As Angron was being transformed into a [[Daemon Prince]] by [[Lorgar]]'s sorcery, Lhorke could not take his Legion's corruption any longer and attacked the [[Word Bearers]] Primarch. However the still-transforming Angron intervened and ripped Lhorke's Dreadnought suit apart.{{Fn|1c}}

Lhurn Adare.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Lhurn Adare'''{{Fn|3f}} was a [[Guardsman]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|3a}}


==Biography==
On [[Sapiencia]], Adare was part of a fire-team that tried to infiltrate the [[hive]] of [[Oskray Island One]] via a breach in [[Oskray Island|the island's]] sea walls. The team was to have been led by [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Gorley]] but he was killed in an artillery bombardment before he could make it inside the wall and so command of the mission fell to Trooper [[Dermon Caffran|Caffran]].{{Fn|2}}

By the time of the regiment's later deployment on [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]], Adare had been promoted and now held the rank of [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] himself.{{Fn|3a}} On the night of his promotion, he and a number of other Tanith went a little overboard while celebrating and ended up getting extremely drunk.{{Fn|3f}}

While on Phantine, he was one of the sixteen Tanith Guardsmen selected personally by [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt|Gaunt]] for participation in [[Operation Larisel]]{{Fn|3b}} and was given command of team Larisel 3. After Larisel 3 successfully infiltrated the [[Blood Pact]]-held city of [[Ouranberg]]{{Fn|3d}}, they tried to make their way through the city by blending in with a work party of enslaved [[Imperial citizen]]s.{{Fn|3e}} However, [[Trooper]]s [[Brin Milo|Milo]] and [[Nessa]] were separated from the group and, while looking for them, Specialist [[Lex Cardinale|Cardinale]] was struck by a Blood Pact slaver with an [[electro-lash]]. This made him drop his [[aquila]] pendant and, when the slavers discovered it, they raised the alarm and unleashed [[cyber-mastiff]]s to track him down. [[Doyl]] and Adare were forced to break cover to save Cardinale from being mauled to death by the hate-dogs and this led to a firefight while they tried to get to safety. Ultimately, Doyl and Adare were cut down by [[loxatl]] [[mercenaries]].{{Fn|3e}}

'''Lhykhis, the Whispering Web''', is an [[Eldar]] [[Phoenix Lord]] and the founder of the [[Warp Spider]] [[Aspect]].{{Fn|1}}

===History===
Lhykhis has been rarely seen in the [[41st Millennium]], leading many [[Imperial]] scholars to consider her apocryphal. At one point, she had been absent for so long that even the Eldar believed her lost. More recently, however, Lhykhis has returned, becoming one of the more active Phoenix Lords and traveling the galaxy to defend her people.{{Fn|2}}

She embodies the [[Eldar]] god [[Khaine]]'s willingness to risk everything for victory and is considered to be a daredevil, even amongst her fellow [[Phoenix Lord]]s. A master of the combat style of her Aspect, she specializes in ambushes and swift, sudden assaults.{{Fn|2}} Despite the dangers of these attacks, Lhykhis is known for repeatedly plunging into the [[Warp]] without fear and uses her keen eye for navigation to go farther and more accurately than even the most ancient [[Warp Spider]] [[Exarch]]s. When the Eldar need her, though, Lhykhis emerges from the Warp to save them from doom, with her unique four-armed [[Aspect Armour]], twin [[Death Weaver]]s known as [[Brood Twain]], twin monofilament injectors dubbed the [[Spider's Fangs]], and the sword [[Vhattarkan]], known as the Weaverender.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}

(Former){{Fn|1}} **[[Inquisition]] ***[[Ordo Hereticus]] **[[Istvaanian]]s |Notes = }} '''Lichtenstein''' is a renowned [[Radical]] [[Istvaanian]] [[Inquisitor]].{{Fn|2c}} Having since been declared '''[[Excommunicate Traitoris]]''', he is currently being actively hunted by one of the most renowned [[Witch Hunter]]s of the Imperium, [[Tyrus]].{{Fn|1}} ===History=== Lichtenstein has a single-minded obsession with the artifact known as the [[Liber Heresius]] that freed the [[Daemon Prince]] [[Phara'gueottla]] from its prison on [[Karis Cephalon]]. Since then, his fate has been inextricably tied with that of Tyrus, the Daemon, and the ex-[[Daemonhost]] known as [[Kessel]]. These three clashed on Karis over the manifestation of the Daemon Prince on the world of [[Paganus Reach]] and again at [[Cephalon]] Spaceport where Lichtenstein managed to break Kessel free from Tyrus' custody. In return, Kessel gave Lichtenstein safe passage to [[Equinox]], a world where, under the false name of '''Thravian Flast''', he searches tirelessly for the true location of the Liber Heresius.{{Fn|1}} Now a very old man, his strength of will allows him to continue on with his mission. While many have dismissed him as mad and traitorous, he sincerely believes that he is on a quest to save mankind from enslavement at the ends of an ancient mechanical race who worship death. Since no one believes him, he has vowed to do it himself. He knows that within the Liber Heresius is a powerful weapon, proof against these ancient killing machines. Lichtenstein will do anything, including harnessing the powers of [[Chaos]], to obtain it.{{Fn|1}} Lichtenstein wield the [[Daemon Weapon#Daemon_Weapons_of_Khorne|Sword of Khorne]] [[Schlack'ta]] that has a [[Bloodletter]] bound within.{{Fn|2b}} At the world of [[Karis Cephalon]], where he was looking for the device called the [[the Angel]], did he come into conflict with Inquisitor [[Kessel]] that was also looking for the Angel, but for other reasons.{{Fn|3}} ===Retinue=== * [[Ghaustos]] ([[Daemonhost]]){{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|4}} * [[Magos Dimitri]] ([[tech-priest]]){{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|4}} * [[Gryx]] ([[Servitor]]-Warrior){{Fn|2a}} ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} * Lichtenstein and his retinue was created by [[Games Workshop]] employee [[Phil Kelly]] in [[White Dwarf 257 (UK)]] for the [[Inquisitor (game)]].{{Fn|2a}} * In [[Dark Heresy: Ascension]] is his name misspelled as "Lichenstein".{{Fn|5}} ===Related Articles=== *[[List of Inquisitors]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Inquisition]], pg. 36 *2: [[White Dwarf 257 (UK)]] **{{Endn|2a}}: pgs. 40-43 - ''Diary of an Inquisitor: the Creation of an Inquisitor Warband'' **{{Endn|2b}}: pg. 41 **{{Endn|2c}}: pgs. 101-115 - ''The Dweller Beneath: an [[Inquisitor (game)]] [[battle report]] by [[Graham McNeill]], [[Phil Kelly]] and [[Rowland Cox]]'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[White Dwarf 264 (UK)]], pgs. 103-118 - ''Battle Report: The Paraelix Configuration'' *{{Endn|4}}: [[White Dwarf 266 (UK)]], pgs. 60-61 - ''A Radical Encounter'' by [[Graham McNeill]] *{{Endn|5}}: [[Dark Heresy: Ascension]], pg. 163 ====Uncited appearances==== *[[Dark Heresy Second Edition: Enemies Without]] pg. 22 [[Category:Characters (Human)]] [[Category:Characters (Inquisition)]] [[fr:Lichtenstein]]

Lijah Cuu.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
{{spoiler|source=Gaunt's Ghosts (Novel Series)}}
'''Lijah Cuu'''{{Fn|1b}} was a [[trooper]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]], the famous ''"[[Ibram Gaunt|Gaunt's]] Ghosts"'', serving in the [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment's]] [[Imperial Guard Platoon|eleventh platoon]].{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
[[Image:CuuArt.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Trooper Cuu{{Fn|5}}]]
Lijah Cuu was a [[Vervunhive]]r [[ganger]] who joined the Tanith First after the [[Siege of Vervunhive]].{{Fn|1b}} A heavily tattooed psychopath with a scar down the centre of his face{{Fn|1b}}, Cuu was a talented tattoo artist{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}} with superb stealth and marksmanship skills (to the point that he was one of the first [[Verghast]]ite members of the regiment to be considered for elevation to the regiment's [[Imperial Guard Scout|scout corps]]{{Fn|2a}}), but his vicious sadism and anti-social behaviour made him unpopular with most of the Ghosts, especially [[Hlaine Larkin|Larkin]], whom he particularly disturbed.{{Fn|1c}}{{Fn|1d}}

During the battle for [[Cirenholm]] on [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]] he looted shops despite the coins being defaced with [[Mark of Khorne|Chaos sigils]]{{Fn|2b}}, and in the aftermath he raped and murdered a young civilian mother and widow, [[Onti Flyte]].{{Fn|2c}} [[Dermon Caffran]] was implicated in the crime and almost executed for it{{Fn|2c}}, but he was let off when Trooper [[Bragg]] reported Cuu's looting after learning that a defaced coin had been found at the crime scene.{{Fn|2d}} Though Cuu escaped conviction for the rape and murder due to insufficient evidence, he was flogged for looting and held a murderous grudge thereafter, hacking Bragg to shreds in a psychotic rage during the final phase of the assault on [[Ouranberg]].{{Fn|2e}}

He then turned his malevolent attentions on Larkin, whom he knew suspected the truth, attempting to murder him twice on [[Aexe Cardinal]] and killing [[Sehra Muril]] after Larkin confided his suspicions to her. He attempted to murder [[Tona Criid]] on [[Herodor]] for no other reason than she was incapacitated and alone, but was prevented by [[Gol Kolea]].{{Fn|3}} Later during the siege of [[Civitas Beati]] Cuu became possessed by [[Rogue Psyker|enemy psykers]], who exploited his evil nature to turn him into a [[Chaos]] pawn.{{Fn|4a}} Whilst under their influence he tried to assassinate [[Saint Sabbat]]{{Fn|4b}}, mowing down Colonel [[Corbec]] during the failed attempt before being fatally headshot by Larkin.{{Fn|4c}}

Lisbeth.wikitext:
'''Lisbeth''', also known as the Iron Angel, was only 16 when she first climbed into the harness of an [[arachni-rig]]. As a young clanner, she and her father joined a group of [[Van Saar]] green hivers heading for a new life in the [[underhive]]. Somewhere down-hive of [[Dust Falls]], they were attacked by mutie raiders, hundreds of starving mutant cannibals pouring out of the shadows to fall upon the uphivers. Lisbeth’s father, a former artisan of the Montari Artifice House, hastened to don his prized arachni-rig but was killed by a stray round, even as young Lisbeth hurried to strap him in. The young Van Saar quickly climbed into the rig herself, and in that first battle found her true calling. When the last mutie finally died howling under her mechanical claws, the battlefield was littered with dead and dismembered raiders, and she was covered from head to toe in their blood. The green hivers hailed her as a hero, and when they finally reached the promised domes outside the [[Bone-dry]] near [[Rust Town]], Lisbeth was already getting offers of work. Less than two cycles later, Lisbeth was known in the underhive of Hive Primus as the Iron Angel, an avenging techno-terror that preys upon outlaws, raiders, and monsters of all kinds. She still works primarily for her own kind, joining Van Saar gangs if their interests align with her own. Mostly, though, she takes jobs to repair her custom arachni-rig or make improvements to it, all the while hunting down the leader of the raiders who killed her father – a rogue psyker known as [[Alyce Shivver]].{{Fn|1}}

Livia.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''Livia Sorken'''{{Fn|3}} is the [[Shipmaster]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[Strike Cruiser]], ''[[Sword of Baal]]''.{{fn|2}}
==History==
[[Image:Livia.jpg|thumb|right|200px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]
She is level headed in a crisis and Livia's willingness to take matters into her own hands has earned the [[Shipmaster]] the [[Chapter]]'s respect. This has allowed her to speak with just as much authority as the [[Blood Angels]] and Livia is not afraid to defend the ''[[Sword of Baal]]'', should they not be aboard it. She was later at the helm of an entire Blood Angels fleet, that was enveloped by the [[Great Rift]]'s birth. The giant [[Warp Storm]] damaged the [[Strike Cruiser]] and killed many of its crew, before only the ''Sword of Baal'' managed to escape back to [[Realspace]]. As the Strike Cruiser found itself stranded above the world [[Niades]] and Livia discovered she had lost her fleet. She now bears the weight of those lost souls heavily.{{Fn|1}}   

==Notes==
''Livia'' is a character in the [[Angels of Death (Animated Series)]].{{Fn|1}}

Loemid.wikitext:
{{ImperialFistsPortal}}
'''Loemid''' was an [[Imperial Fist]], who took part in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1}} 
==History==
He was later among the [[Imperial Fists]]{{Fn|1}} that the [[Loyalist Legion|Legion]]'s [[Primarch]], [[Rogal Dorn]], commanded as part of the [[Emperor]]'s [[Teleportation]] boarding attack upon the [[Sons of Horus]]' flagship, the [[Vengeful Spirit]].{{Fn|2a}} They were tasked with killing the [[Traitor|traitorous]] Primarch [[Horus]], in order to save [[Terra]] and the [[Imperium]], but due to Horus' machinations, the Emperor's boarding party was separated from each other.{{Fn|2b}} Worse still for the Imperial Fists aboard the Vengeful Spirit, Dorn had also been torn away from them{{Fn|2c}} and so the [[Huscarls (Imperial Fists)|Huscarl]] [[Diamantis]] took command of the Legion's forces. However the Imperial Forces would all be killed, after they were swarmed by Horus' forces and their remains were later found by a grief stricken Rogal Dorn, who swore to avenge their deaths.{{Fn|1}}

Logris.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Logris''' was a [[Imperial Guard Scout|Scout-Trooper]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment]] who served under [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Mkoll]].{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
When the Tanith First were deployed on [[Caligula (Hive World)|Caligula]], Logris was part of a detachment assigned to escort a supply convoy from [[Aurelian Hive]] to [[Hive Calphernia]], manning the [[Autocannon|guns]] of an outrider driven by [[Fulke]]. When the convoy was attacked by bandits, however, Fulke tried to flee in a panic and Logris was forced to knock him unconscious and take control of the vehicle himself.{{Fn|1a}}

Later when the Tanith were fielded against [[Chaos Cultists]] on [[Monthax]], Logris was attached to the regiment's [[Imperial Guard Platoon|Third Platoon]] under [[Major]] [[Elim Rawne]]. Unbeknownst to the Guard, however, a group of [[Aeldari]] was also active on Monthax. The [[Warlock]] [[Eon Kull]] [[Psyker|conjured]] a massive storm in order to hide their activities and the Tanith were caught in the middle of it; Logris was hit in the neck by a severed tree branch and killed instantly.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|Conflicting sources}}


==Trivia==
{{Trivia}}

*In the novel [[Ghostmaker (Novel)|Ghostmaker]], Logris is killed during the [[Monthax]] campaign. Despite this, the following novel, [[Necropolis (Novel)|Necropolis]], shows Logris as amongst a unit of Tanith under [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Varl]] and [[Corporal]] [[Meryn]] active during the [[Siege of Vervunhive]].{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2b}}

Lokris.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
[[General]] '''Lokris''' was a senior officer of the [[Imperial Guard]].

==Biography==
Lokris was more than a hundred years old in or around 928.[[M41]], when [[Commissar]] [[Ciaphas Cain]] was promoted away from the [[Valhallan 12th Field Artillery]] to the Imperial force's brigade headquarters.  A firm believer in Cain's heroic reputation, he often assigned Cain to the most dangerous missions{{Fn|1}}.

Despite this, Cain developed a liking for Lokris, finding him a refreshingly direct and honest man, who shared Cain's low tolerance for bureacracy and office politicking.  Cain also appreciated the talents of Lokris' personal chef and the quality of his private store of [[amasec]], both of which Cain was able to enjoy thanks to his favored position (between episodes of "bowel-clenching terror."){{Fn|2a}}

In spite of his advanced age, Lokris was always eager for action, which led him to volunteer to command the campaign on [[Archipelaga]] against [[heretic]] insurgents{{Fn|2a}}.  During this deployment, he assigned Cain to what looked like a routine search mission, which led to uncovering a [[Nurgle|Nurglite]] [[Chaos cult|cult]] on the planet{{Fn|2b}}.

Lorenz.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''Lorenz''' was a member of the of the [[Blood Angels]], who was among the same [[Aspirant]] group that [[Commander Dante]] was a part of in 456.[[M40]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
He became good friends with [[Dante]] and a fellow Aspirant named [[Florian]], after they met each other during their journey to reach [[Angel's Fall]] on [[Baal Secundus]]. They passed the [[Blood Angels]]' trials there{{Fn|1a}} and were then taken in a group with other successful Aspirants to the [[Chapter]]'s '''Place of Challenge''', where they underwent further trials. There they were joined by a different group of Aspirants from [[Baal Primus]], and the officers overseeing the trials told the group that though they were from different worlds, the Aspirants had to learn to work together and grow bonds with each other, if they wished to pass the upcoming trials. A surly Lorenz refused to do this at first, claiming that as he was the group's strongest warrior, he could pass the trials without needing to. It was only after constant prodding by Dante and Florian, that Lorenz finally relented and began socializing with the Baal Primus Aspirants{{Fn|1b}}. Eventually Lorenz and Dante both passed the Aspirant trials to become [[Neophytes]]{{Fn|1c}} and the two would then go on to advance through the Blood Angel's ranks, all while fighting side by side together.{{Fn|1d}}

{{Character |Portal ={{SonsOfHorusPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image = |Caption = |Title = |Homeworld = |Birth =c. [[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - 008.[[M31]] |Death =008.[[M31]], [[Dagonet]] |Cause of Death =Killed by the [[Vindicare Assassin]] [[Eristede Kell]] |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Horus]]
("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation =[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Sons of Horus]] [[13th Company (Sons of Horus)|13th Company]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by =[[Zistrion]] (As 13th Company Captain) |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] (Former) **[[Sons of Horus]] ***[[13th Company (Sons of Horus)|13th Company]] *[[Dark Empire]] |Notes = }} '''Luc Sedirae''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[13th Company (Sons of Horus)|13th Company]] of the [[Sons of Horus]] (formerly Luna Wolves) [[Space Marine Legion]].{{fn|1a}} ===Biography=== A notable warrior, Luc Sedirae's martial exploits were considered to be not far behind those of [[First Captain]] [[Ezekyle Abaddon]].{{Fn|1b}} Sedirae was considered at one point for elevation into the [[Mournival]] brotherhood, but was passed over in favour of [[Garviel Loken]]. The rumoured reason for this was that he was considered too ruthless in battle and too eager an advocate of warfare. The [[Primarch]] [[Rogal Dorn]] talked of Sedirae as a battle-hungry killer ready to say yes to any plan that would lead to glory in combat.{{Fn|1c}} It is likely therefore, that his opinion would have unbalanced the Mournival's council and was therefore deemed unsuitable.{{fn|1b}} Despite his fearsome reputation as a combatant, in person Luc Sedirae was seen as charming, friendly, charismatic and handsome. Blonde-haired and blue-eyed, he always seemed to be smiling, although sometimes his habit of keeping his mouth half-open gave the impression that he was just about to bite something.{{fn|1d}} Sedirae often deployed himself in an assault role, and therefore wore a [[jump pack]] upon occasion.{{Fn|2b}} Sedirae took part in many notable campaigns during the [[Great Crusade]]. On the world of [[Murder]], he achieved glory in leading his company against a force of [[Megarachnids|Megarachnid]] over 2,500 strong; 13th Company shattered the Megarachnid force in half an hour.{{Fn|1e}} He fought the unnatural forces of 'Nurg-leth' on the moon of [[Davin]], saving Garviel Loken at one point{{fn|2a}} and leading the assault on the ''Glory of Terra'' at another{{fn|2b}}. During the assault on the downed starship Sedirae and his cohort were cut off from their fellows and found themselves in close combat with [[Nurgle]] [[daemons]]. This experience seemed to unnerve the [[Sons of Horus]] Captain.{{Fn|2c}} A firm believer in the [[warrior-lodge]] and a companion to [[Serghar Targost]], Luc Sedirae willingly followed the direction of his Primarch and co-commanded the initial Sons of Horus deployments against the loyalist marines upon [[Isstvan III]].{{Fn|3}} Sedirae was later present on the planet [[Dagonet]] in the [[Segmentum Ultima]]. The planet had been the site of one of [[Horus]]'s first conquests, in which he claimed the planet for the [[Imperium]] with a single bolter shot. After a lengthy civil war seemed to have died down, with the pro-Horus aristocracy emerging on top, Dagonet declared for the Warmaster. To commemorate the event, Horus came to the system to attend a ceremony in which the planet welcomed Horus as its twice-come liberator from oppression.{{Fn|4a}} However, it was Sedirae who descended to the planet in Horus's place, acting as his body-double and wearing the Warmaster's regalia. This choice saved Horus's life, as upon removing his helm, [[Execution Force|a team]] of [[Imperial Assassin|assassins]] led by the [[Vindicare]] sniper [[Eristede Kell]] managed to kill the unsuspecting Sedirae.{{Fn|4a}}{{Fn|4b}} ===Aftermath=== Angered, the Sons of Horus killed the entire aristocracy in a matter of moments, and then turned its aggression against the entirety of the planet, leaving little of the population left alive. The relatively few survivors were then rounded up and ritually sacrificed to Chaos.{{Fn|4b}}{{Fn|4c}} Sedirae's 13th Company was especially eager in these massacres, as its members wanted to take revenge for their slain Captain.{{Fn|4b}}{{Fn|7}} Sedirae was succeeded by his subordinate [[Jerrod]], who was also considered for the Mournival; however, Jerrod was turned down due to his recent command being too new to effectively perform both his job as 13th Company Captain and the advisory position of the council.{{Fn|5}} Jerrod would later be succeeded himself by [[Zistrion]], who was considered to be a poor copy of his predecessors.{{Fn|6}} ===Sources=== *1: [[Horus Rising (Novel)]]: **{{endn|1a}}: ''Dramatis Personae'' **{{endn|1b}}: Part One, ch. 3 **{{endn|1c}}: Part One, ch. 6 **{{endn|1d}}: Part One, ch. 7 **{{endn|1e}}: Part Two, ch. 7 *2: [[False Gods (Novel)]]: **{{endn|2a}}: ch. 6 **{{endn|2b}}: ch. 7 **{{endn|2c}}: ch. 8 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Galaxy In Flames (Novel)]], ch. 16 *4: [[Nemesis (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|4a}}: Part 2, Chapter 14 **{{Endn|4b}}: Part 2, Chapter 15 **{{Endn|4c}}: Part 2, Chapter 18 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Little Horus (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|6}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume I (Novel)]], 4:ix *{{Endn|7}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Six - Retribution]], pg. 207 {{DEFAULTSORT:Sedirae, Luc}} [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Sons of Horus)]] [[de:Luc Sedirae]]

[[Image:Calsius.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Lieutenant Calsius]]
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Lieutenant (Space Marine)|Lieutenant]] in the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter|Chapter's]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] and a veteran of the [[Indomitus Crusade]], where he received his current rank. Due to being a relative newcomer to his Chapter, Calsius works hard to earn the respect of his [[Battle Brother]]s and has displayed bravery and wisdom in numerous battles. Besides the Indomitus Crusade, Calsius has also taken part in the [[Plague Wars]] and defeated an [[Ork]] attack on the [[Agri World]] [[Nova Thulium]].{{Fn|1a}} His celebrated victory there, including personally killing the [[Warboss]] [[Guttrekk]], proved to be the turning point that allowed the Imperium's forces to defeat an Ork invasion of the [[Ultramar|Realm of Ultramar's]] eastern flank.{{Fn|1b}}

He is currently leading a strike force to aid the [[Imperium]] world [[Korvon II]]{{Fn|2}}, which has been invaded by the [[Death Guard]]{{Fn|3}}, his most hated foes.{{Fn|1a}}

(As Captain of the 2nd Company) |Faction ='' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Realm of Ultramar]] **[[Ultramarines]] ***[[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] |Notes = }} '''Lucian Trajan''' was a former [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]]'s [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]].{{Fn|1}} ==History== He served as its [[First Sergeant]], when the [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd]] was led by [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Severus Agemman]], during the [[First Tyrannic War]]. However the [[Space Marine Company|Company]] was fighting elsewhere, when the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Adeptus Astartes Homeworld|Homeworld]], [[Macragge]], was invaded by [[Hive Fleet Behemoth]]. Though the 2nd raced to aid their [[Chapter]], they arrived after victory had been achieved at Macragge and the Company instead joined the [[Imperial]] reinforcements that helped in scouring [[Ultramar]]'s worlds of the [[Hive Fleet]]'s presence. As this occurred, the Ultramarines began to rebuild their devastated Chapter and Agemman was made the Captain of the [[1st Company (Ultramarines)|1st Company]]. Trajan would then become the 2nd's Captain and [[Demetrian Titus]] became the [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergent]] of his [[Space Marine Command Squad|Command Squad]]. The 2nd would then continue to aid in the effort to purge Ultramar of Hive Fleet Behemoth's remnants.{{Fn|1}} For a century afterwards, Trajan and [[Demetrian Titus|Titus]] not only fought together, but also flourished under the tutelage they received from [[First Captain]] [[Severus Agemman]]. However this ended, when the [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] was sent to aid the besieged [[Imperial]] world [[Beta-Arcturus]]. It had been invaded by the [[Asuryani]] forces of [[Craftworld]] [[Biel-Tan]] and once the 2nd arrived, Trajan led a [[Space Marine Company|Demi-Company]] against the [[Xenos]]' [[Autarch]] leader. The Captain then killed the Autarch in single combat, as Titus and his [[Space Marine Command Squad|Command Squad]] kept the Xenos leader's [[Aspect Warrior]] bodyguards at bay. Their Autarch's death caused Biel-Tan's surviving forces to retreat, but as they did so the Xenos captured the [[Ultramarine]] [[Leandros]]. This led Trajan to give command of the Company to Titus, so that he could lead a combat squad to free the young warrior. Leandros was merely bait to lure the Captain into a trap, though, and Trajan's squad was ambushed by Biel-Tan's hidden reserve forces. The Captain was then surrounded by the Xenos and mercilessly killed. After learning of this, Titus was able to lead the 2nd in an attack that finally drove off the Xenos from Beta-Arcturus and Leandros and Trajan's body were recovered.{{Fn|1}} Upon the [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]]'s return to [[Macragge]], Trajan was placed in a grand sepulchre within the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Fortress of Hera]]. Its [[Chapter Master]], [[Marneus Calgar]], then decided to make [[Demetrian Titus|Titus]] the 2nd's new [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]]. While some of his [[Battle Brothers]] had thought it was a rank he was suited for, Titus had never sought to rise to such heights. He had been content with his position as [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] and had only wished to serve Trajan and the [[Emperor]] in whatever way was asked of him. While Titus accepted becoming the 2nd Company's Captain,{{Fn|1}} he felt the weight of taking over his predecessor's mantle.{{Fn|2}} ==See Also== *[[List of Space Marine Captains]] ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[White Dwarf 498]], pgs. 54-56 - ''Lieutenant Titus of the Ultramarines'' *{{Endn|2}}: [https://web.archive.org/web/20111210083405/http://www.spacemarine.com/game/characters/single-player WH40K: Space Marine, Single Player characters] ''(archived page, last accessed via Wayback Machine 24 September 2021)'' {{DEFAULTSORT:Trajan, Lucian}} [[Category:Characters (Ultramarines)]] [[Category:Characters (Tyrannic Wars)]] [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]]

***[[Aeronautica Imperialis]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a legendary [[Imperial Navy]] flying ace.{{Fn|1}} ==Biography== Lucille von Shard has been described as the 'prodigal daughter' of the [[von Shard]] family.{{Fn|3b}} Lucille is one of seven siblings, all of whom went through the [[Schola Progenium]] following the deaths of their parents; [[Horotha Shard]] (a [[Colonel]] of the [[Verlaian One Hundred and Fifth Regiment|Verlaian 105th]]) and [[Tazinia Shard]] (a [[Tank Commander]] in the [[Nauticium One Hundred and Twelfth|Nauticium 112th]]).{{Fn|2c}} She does not get on well with her sister [[Josephine von Shard|Josephine]].{{Fn|3c}} Of her brothers; [[Tobia von Shard|Tobia]], is an [[Imperial]] [[Commissar]] and had worked with [[Propagandist]] [[Kile Simlex]] before.{{Fn|2c}}{{Fn|3c}} [[Rile von Shard|Rile]],{{Fn|3q}} is an [[Inquisitorial]] [[Acolyte]]{{Fn|3t}} under [[Inquisitor]] [[Ortis Atenbach]],{{Fn|3u}} and [[Maric von Shard|Maric]] is a [[Confessor]].{{Fn|2c}} ===Bacchus=== {{Spoiler|source=Outgunned (Novel)}} Lucille von Shard led the [[2208th Expeditionary Air Wing]] in the air war on [[Bacchus]].{{Fn|2b}} Where she fought an [[Ork]] airship. Here she met the [[Imperial]] [[propagandist]] [[Kile Simlex]].{{Fn|3d}} ===Deighton=== {{Spoiler|source=Above and Beyond (Novel)}} After the events of [[Bacchus]] Lucille von Shard had been left a broken woman, often turning to alcohol,{{Fn|3g}} and having trouble sleeping.{{Fn|3j}} At some point after the Bacchus campaign Lucille went on a drunken rant where she exclaimed her disdain for the Imperium, and even damned the God-Emperor. This was all recorded by [[Propagandist]] [[Emulle Esec]].{{Fn|3r}} The first real challenge to [[Imperial]] air superiority on [[Deighton]] came from a [[Separatist]] ace, known as the [[Desert Wind]].{{Fn|4a}} Propagandist Esec, who had been using Lucille von Shard’s image to promote Imperial propaganda on the world. Deighton had a data stream shared by the [[Data Fortress]]es named [[The Feed]], which Esec used to share shortform minute long [[pict]]s with the local populace.{{Fn|3f}} Esec was overjoyed at the appearance of the Desert Wind, so that he capture picts of a dog-fight between the two ace pilots.{{Fn|4a}} Alongside [[Wing Sergeant]] [[Vagbon]], and seven other [[Lightning]]s, Lucille von Shard took to the air over the [[Great Glass Plain]].{{Fn|4b}} [[Auspex]] detected six enemy [[Thunderbolt]] fighters, and the Imperials raced to engage them. Vagbon spotted the Desert Wind but, as she lined up a kill shot, Esec cut into the [[vox]] to order her to hold fire, so that it could be Lucille von Shard who would finish off the enemy Ace. It was then that a bright light engulfed the battle, blinding Vagbon.{{Fn|4c}} Despite her earlier dismisal and disdain of Vagbon,{{Fn|4a}} when von Shard saw her wingman in trouble she immediately acted, and instructed Vagbon on how to recover. The Desert Wind was shot down, though Esec was unable to capture a pict of it due to the interference.{{Fn|4d}} Esec then came up with the idea of having Vagbon, and others, fly while in [[Lightning]]s marked with von Shard's colours; a major faux pas among [[Imperial Navy|Navy]] pilots. This owuld allow him to get more picts, without having to rely on the unreliable Lucille von Shard.{{Fn|3j}}{{Fn|4d}} Shortly after his pict of Lucille von Shard shooting down the Desert Wind, in reality Vagbon sparring with a repainted Imperial Thunderbolt,{{Fn|4d}} was uploaded to The Feed, the Data Fortress of [[Edbar]] opened its gates to the Imperial forces without a fight.{{Fn|3f}} Lucille von Shard was reunited with [[Imperial]] [[propagandist]] [[Kile Simlex]]{{Fn|3g}}, now [[scribe]] following his demotion after his work on the [[pict|cinema-pict]], [[The 2208]], which had shown the reality of war before it has been reedited.{{Fn|3b}} Their previous parting on Bacchus having left both parties feeling hostile to each other.{{Fn|3h}} Following an attack by the [[xenos]] [[mercenary]] [[Cesh]] during the filming of a propaganda pict, Lucille von Shard took to the sky to attempt to shoot the [[aeldari]] pilot down, despite being drunk and sleep deprived. She managed to score a single [[lascannon]] hit on the aeldari aircraft, though did not shoot it down. {{Fn|3j}} Despite the loss of over twenty [[Thunderbolt]] and [[Lightning]] fighters to the single aeldari aircraft, Lucille von Shard claimed the dogfight a great victory. Something which disgusted Scribe Simlex.{{Fn|3k}} Following the dogfight Cesh started to release his own propaganda on [[The Feed]], claiming Lucille von Shard to be an unskilled coward, and the Imperial forces on Deighton to be imposters. He promised to shoot Lucille von Shard down in five days time.{{Fn|3k}} When [[Commissar]] [[Tobia von Shard]]'s attack in the tunnels below Deighton faltered, after [[Cesh]] destroyed a [[Hellhound]] tank, Lucille von Shard was ordered by Propagandist Esec to fly her [[Lightning]] into the tunnels to engage the aeldari pilot. Lucille, however, opted to instead lead a squadron of [[Valkyrie]]s. This enraged Propagandist Esec, who was focused on capturing a heroic pict more than on good tactical sense. He continued to order [[Láech]] [[guardsmen]] out to their deaths to confirm the aeldari aircraft was still there while waiting over an hour for Lucille von Shard’s arrival. As the squadron approached the aeldari's position Scribe Simlex informed Lucille von Shard that he brother was missing in action, presumed dead from the aeldari's attack.{{Fn|3l}} When the Valkyries arrived at the battle, Propagandist Esec ordered [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Xvier]] to his death to flush the aeldari out. When the Sergeant was killed Lucille von Shard and her squadron fired all weapons they had. However as they continued to advance Cesh shot down all of the Valkyries except for Lucille's, reminding her that it was not yet time for him to shoot her down.{{Fn|3l}} A day after the battle in the tunnels Cesh again went live on The Feed to show Lucille von Shard that he had captured her brother, [[Tobia von Shard]], promising to spare his life in return for the one on one aerial duel he sought with her.{{Fn|3m}} [[Flight Sergeant]] [[Petre Plient]] and Lucille von Shard got to work on preparing for the aerial combat.{{Fn|3n}} In the meantime Propagandist Esec received a seperate communication offering the coordinates of the Commissar and dispatched Scribe Simlex to retrieve the Commissar{{Fn|3o}}, though it would be revealed that Cesh never had the Commissar, it was feint. Lucille von Shard used the negotiations as cover to launch an attack against Cesh. Cesh had expected this and attacked the Imperial aricraft, revealing he had a flight of allied aeldari aircraft with him and was not alone, as had previously been thought. The aeldari shot down several [[Avenger]] Strike Fighters and at least one [[Lightning]] painted in Lucille von Shard's colours. Lucille von Shard herself was piloting a different [[Lightning]] and was able to shoot down one of the aeldari aircraft.{{Fn|3o}} Following the engagment Flight Sergeant Plient organsied a dinner with Lucille von Shard and Scribe Simlex. Though the two still held disdain for each other, they agreed to have the dinner to avoid hurting Plient. Lucille and Simlex seemed to warm slightly during the dinner, and Lucille offered to walk the Scribe home afterwards.{{Fn|3p}} During the walk Simlex informed Lucille that Cesh never had her brother as a prisoner and that, in all likelyhood, the Commissar was dead. Lucille dismissed this, stating her brother had survived worse, she then invited Simlex to her personal quarters.{{Fn|3q}} Here she showed him the footage Propagandist Esec had captured of her drunken rant against the Imperium and the God-Emperor, revealing to Simlex why Esec had so much power over her.{{Fn|3r}} The following day Cesh sent coordinates for their duel. The [[Mendax Matertera]] burst from the sky, modified by [[Flight Sergeant]] [[Petre Plient|Plient]], and opened fire on the aeldari. Despite superficial damage to the aeldari craft, the Mendax Matertera was swiftly shot down, and Lucille feared dead.{{Fn|3s}} After the duel Scribe Simlex encountered [[Acolyte]] [[Rile von Shard]]. The Acolyte revealed he has saved Commissar von Shard's life.{{Fn|3t}} Acolyte von Shard and Simlex travelled to the crash site of where they recovered Flight Sergeant Plient's [[augmetic]] arm from the wreck.{{Fn|3u}} Lucille has not piloted Mendax Matertera, and had instead escaped. Plient had told Lucille he had made a [[servitor]] pilot the [[Lightning]], and she was unaware of his death, until Simlex caught up with her and informed her of the truth.{{Fn|3v}} ==Equipment== [[Image:MendaxMatertera.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Lightning]] fighter: [[Mendax Matertera]].{{Fn|2a}}]] Lucille von Shard pilots the [[Lightning]] [[Mendax Matertera]], or ''Black Griffon''. The aircraft features a sandy-white camoflauge scheme, with a bright blue underbelly.{{Fn|3i}} It has a pair of black griffons painted on the wings,{{Fn|3i}}{{Fn|4b}} and is armed with a single [[Autocannon]] and two [[Lascannons]]. Lucille von Shard hangs [[Kile Simlex]]'s former [[Servo-skull|seer-skull]], [[Kikazar]], from one wing as a good luck charm.{{Fn|3i}} During one of her duels with [[Cesh]], [[Flight Sergeant]] [[Petre Plient|Plient]] welded four additional autocannons to the Lightning and an unknown number of missiles above the wings. [[Scribe]] [[Kile Simlex|Simlex]] noted that the loadout would probably have been considered [[heretical]] by the [[Tech-Priests]]. Mendax Matertera was destroyed during this duel.{{Fn|3s}} ==Appearances in Black Library Works== Lucille von Shard appears in the following [[Black Library]] publications: *[[The Trial of Lucille von Shard (Short Story)]] *[[Outgunned (Novel)]] *[[Starstruck (Short Story)]] *[[Own Worst Enemy (Short Story)]] *[[Above and Beyond (Novel)]] ==Trivia== {{Trivia}} *Lucille's [[Lightning]], [[Mendax Matertera]], is often described as having an underbelly [[autocannon]] and wing mounted [[lascannon]]s in the novels. Matching the appearance of the original [[Forge World]] Lightning fighter model.{{Fn|2c}} However all images of [[Mendax Matertera]] show the craft as a [[Lightning#Voss_Pattern_Lightning_Strike_Fighter|Voss Pattern Lightning Strike Fighter]] which does not have an autocannon at all, and the lascannons are mounted in the nose, rather than on the wings. In addition, artwork shows two large black eagle-like wings painted on the wings of the aircraft,{{Fn|2a}}{{Endn|3a}} though in the novels it is described as having a black griffon inside of a red circle on each wing.{{Fn|2c}} ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2022/08/07/sunday-preview-massed-reinforcements-for-warhammer-the-horus-heresy/ Warhammer Community: Sunday Preview – Massed Reinforcements for Warhammer: The Horus Heresy (Posted on 07/08/2022)] (Last accessed on 7 August 2022) *2: [[Outgunned (Novel)]] (Hard Cover): **{{Endn|2a}}: Front Cover **{{Endn|2b}}: ''Preface'', pgs. 7-8 **{{Endn|2c}}: ''Chapter Two'', pgs. 23-25 *3:[[Above and Beyond (Novel)]] (Hard Cover): **{{Endn|3a}}: Front Cover **{{Endn|3b}}: ''Preface'', pgs. 9-11 **{{Endn|3c}}: ''Chapter One'', pg. 14 **{{Endn|3d}}: ''Chapter Two'', pgs. 19-21 **{{Endn|3e}}: ''Chapter Three'', pg. 27 **{{Endn|3f}}: ''Chapter Seven'', pg. 54 **{{Endn|3g}}: ''Chapter Nine'', pgs. 70-71 **{{Endn|3h}}: ''Chapter Ten'', pg. 81 **{{Endn|3i}}: ''Chapter Fourteen'', pgs. 112-113 **{{Endn|3j}}: ''Chapter Nineteen'', pgs. 141-149 **{{Endn|3k}}: ''Chapter Twenty'', pgs. 152-154 **{{Endn|3l}}: ''Chapter Twenty-Four'' **{{Endn|3m}}: ''Chapter Twenty-Six'' **{{Endn|3n}}: ''Chapter Twenty-Seven'' **{{Endn|3o}}: ''Chapter Twenty-Eight'' **{{Endn|3p}}: ''Chapter Thirty'' **{{Endn|3q}}: ''Chapter Thirty-One'' **{{Endn|3r}}: ''Chapter Thirty-Two'' **{{Endn|3s}}: ''Chapter Thirty-Three'' **{{Endn|3t}}: ''Chapter Thirty-Five'' **{{Endn|3u}}: ''Chapter Thirty-Seven'' **{{Endn|3v}}: ''Chapter Forty'' *4:[[Own Worst Enemy (Short Story)]] (eBook): **{{Endn|4a}}"~ first quarter of the story" **{{Endn|4b}}"~ second quarter of the story" **{{Endn|4c}}"~ third quarter of the story" **{{Endn|4d}}"~ final quarter of the story" {{DEFAULTSORT:Shard, Lucille von}} [[Category:Characters (Imperial Navy)]] [[Category:Characters (Human)]]

Lucius Antros.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Lexicanium]] in the [[Blood Angels]] [[Chapter]] and was the protégé of [[Chief Librarian]] [[Mephiston]].{{Fn|1a}}. Antros served as a close aide to Mephiston and was entrusted with stewardship over the Orbicular Tower within the [[Librarius.]]

Antros accompanied Mephiston to the shrine world [[Divinus Prime]], where the Chief Librarian sought to investigate psychic disturbances and uncover the nature of the Black Rage. Throughout the campaign, Antros remained at Mephiston’s side, assisting in psychic rituals and battlefield operations. His loyalty and competence earned him further trust, though his rapid ascent drew criticism from senior Librarians, most notably [[Epistolary]] [[Gaius Rhacelus]], who viewed Antros as overly ambitious and deferential toward Mephiston.

He was present when [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]] [[Devastation of Baal|invaded]] the [[Baal System]].{{Fn|1a}} However, the Lexicanum would not take part in most of the campaign against the [[Tyranids]]; instead Antros was among the [[Librarian]]s chosen to aid Mephiston in a [[Warp]] ritual that would prevent the [[Bloodthirster]] [[Ka'Bandha]] from invading Baal as well. He was unaware, though, that his inclusion in Mephiston's plan greatly annoyed the Epistolary, who had always felt that Antros was too ambitious and thought it unseemly how the Lexicanum constantly fussed over Mephiston. The Epistolary had even brought his concerns about Antros to the Chief Librarian's attention, but Mephiston ignored any criticisms about his protégé. When the Librarians ventured into [[Baal]]'s '''Cruor Mountains''', where the ritual would take place, Gaius forcibly rebuked himself for doubting Antros,{{Fn|1b}}

Later when the ritual began, a portal into [[Khorne]]'s kingdom was opened and Mephiston struck at Ka'Bandha, in the hopes of ending the [[Daemon]]'s threat before it could escape from the Warp. The Bloodthirster struck back, however, and then offered immortal life to any of the Librarians that revoked their vows to the [[Emperor]]. Though none answered, Antros was falling under the Bloodthirster's sway, but luckily Gaius saw this and quickly told the Lexicanum not to fall for the [[Daemon]]'s false promises. This helped Antros regain his senses, but his weakness left a flaw in the ritual and when Ka'Bandha attacked again, the Librarians collapsed and the Warp portal was closed. Many of the Librarians who took part in the ritual were killed by the ordeal, though Antros himself survived to continue to serve the chapter.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|2a}}
